data.description: Named datasets for layers (`requires.data`), as site-relative paths.

custom.description: Custom layers saved in this site, by id. A scene uses one as `custom:<id>`.

palette.description: The table's colours (#93): a built-in set and the slots this table changes.

services.description:
Outside compute the table's layers reach through the host (#278): programs the host
starts beside the table (a Python model in its own venv) or addresses it forwards to.

data_licences.description:
Where the table's data came from and on what terms (#731): sources, licences, credits
and whether a file may travel with the table. See `data_licences.rs`.

rotation_deg.description: Bearing of the table's "up" edge, clockwise from north.

front.description:
The edge of the projected image where visitors stand. At-a-glance info goes there first,
because for a viewer at the front the model hides what is projected on the far side.

ribbons.description: What the projector's blank space around the model shows, per side (present.md, Ribbon).

glow.description: A soft glow in the projector's blank space in the model's own colours (#476, present.md, Ambient glow).

intro.description:
How the projected table opens when it starts and after the controller's Reset: the layers
fading in one after another (the default) or the zoom in from the city around it (#446).

TableSide.description: A side of the projected image.

Ribbon.description: One side's ribbon: `"off"`, `"auto"` (use the free band when there is one) or a size.

Glow.description: The ambient glow around the model: the colours along the model's edges, or one colour for all of it.

strength.description: 0 to 1: how bright the glow is at the model's edge.

oneOf.description: Each edge glows in the colours along it.
The whole margin glows in the model's dominant colour.
The layers at rest fade in one after another, bottom first, each part of a layer a moment after the one before.
The map starts zoomed out over the city around the table and slowly zooms in (#446).

water.description: Water: a river, a lake, the sea (#343). Cool ground for thermal comfort, and a sink for stormwater.

context.description:
Buildings around the table that only shape the wind (#488): footprints reaching past the
table's edge. Nothing draws them.

surfaces.description:
What covers the ground and the soil under it (#624): where stormwater soaks in, runs fast
or drains away. Left out, the site's `roads`, `streets` and `walkways` datasets are read
as OpenStreetMap surfaces; `[]` reads none.

extrude.description:
Whether the footprints are raised into the top surface. Turn off when a mesh
provides the building shapes and the footprints are only drawn.

Terrain.description:
Ground elevation. Either a GeoTIFF (`.tif`, `.tiff`), placed by its own georeference,
or raw little-endian f32 elevations covering the extent, row 0 at the top, which
need `width` and `height`.

crs.description: `EPSG:<code>` of a GeoTIFF that does not name its coordinate system itself.

flatten_buildings.description:
The terrain has the buildings raised in it (a surface model, #344): the ground under each
footprint, and one cell around it, is set back to the ground beside it when baking.

Mesh.description:
A 3D model of the site's top surface (ground and buildings), rasterised into the dsm.
A mesh has no georeference of its own, so the manifest places it.

path.description: An STL (binary or ASCII), OBJ or GLB file.

up.description: Which of the file's axes points up. CAD and 3D printing use Z, glTF and many modelling tools Y.

mirror.description: Whether the model is a mirror image (its X axis is flipped), as some exports are.

offset.description:
A model in map coordinates (#344): this point of the file, in its own units with the
up axis made Z, is taken as its origin, so the numbers stay small. The anchor is where it lies.

anchor.description: Where the mesh's own origin (0, 0) is, after `offset`.

bearing_deg.description: Compass bearing of the mesh's +Y axis, clockwise from north. +X is 90 degrees clockwise from +Y.

base_m.description: Elevation of the mesh's z = 0, in the terrain's height datum.

ground_tolerance_m.description:
The mesh's ground never matches the terrain exactly. Cells where the mesh is less
than this above the terrain stay ground instead of becoming low obstacles.

Up.description: The up axis of a mesh file.

oneOf.description: Y up, Z towards the viewer: read as (x, -z, y).

Water.description: Where the water is: GeoJSON polygons, or a GeoTIFF mask (cells above 0.5 are water).

crs.description: `EPSG:<code>` of a GeoTIFF mask that does not name its coordinate system itself.

WindContext.description: Footprints around the table, for the wind kernel only (#488).

path.description: GeoJSON footprints. Those inside the table are left to `buildings`.

reach_m.description: How far past the table's edge they count, in metres.

SurfaceSource.description: One source of ground surfaces or soils (#624). Exactly one of `data` and `path`.

data.description: A dataset of the site, by its name in `data` (or `roads`, `trees`… of the scene).

path.description: Or a file in the site folder: GeoJSON, or a GeoTIFF of class codes.

property.description:
The property that names the surface or soil, for `kind` (default `kind`) and `soil`
(default: SGU's `jg2_tx`, else the first text property that names a soil).

size_m.description: How wide a point is on the ground, metres. Default by surface: a drain 1, a rain garden 4, else 3.

crs.description: `EPSG:<code>` of a GeoTIFF that does not name its coordinate system itself.

SurfaceClasses.description: How a surface source names what is on the ground (#624).

oneOf.description:
OpenStreetMap tags: `surface`, `landuse`, `leisure`, `natural`, `amenity`, `highway`. Roads and
paths (lines) are laid at a width for their class, or their `width` tag.
Naturvårdsverket's Nationella marktäckedata: a GeoTIFF of NMD class codes.
Soil types under the surface: SGU's soil map (Jordarter, `jg2_tx`), or soil names in English.
A property naming the surface outright: `rain garden`, `drain`, `asphalt`, `grass`… (a field walk's kinds).

style.description: A MapLibre style URL, or null for no basemap.

use.description:
What the instance runs: a core layer id, a relative path to a site-only layer package,
or `custom:<id>` for a custom layer saved in the site's `custom`.

id.description: Names this instance. Unique in the whole scene, items included; steps and the session refer to it.

button.description: How the layer is offered on the controller. What is left out comes from the layer package.

hide.description: Ids of the layer's controls that the controller and phones do not show. The editor still does.

items.description:
Instances that belong to this layer: shown while it is open, gone when it closes.
Drawn on top of it, in this order.

steps.description: How Next moves through the layer, and for a sequence (a slideshow) the steps themselves.

LayerButton.description:
The button that opens a layer on the controller: the words and icon the site's
author chose for it, and where on the controller it sits.

icon.description: An icon name from the editor's set, such as `sun` or `route`.

group.description: The group of buttons it sits in on its rail, such as "Simulations".

order.description: Its place in the rail; lower first. Buttons without one follow the scene order.

hidden.description: Kept off the controller and phones without taking the layer out of the table (#58).

credit.description:
Who made what the layer shows, as one line under its name on the controller (#659),
such as "Artwork by Vishvi Rajakaruna and Fabio Latino".

legend.description: How the controller shows the layer's legend (#660). Without it, `auto`.

LegendMode.description: How much of a layer's legend the controller shows (#660).

oneOf.description: Every row, in as many columns as it takes to fit the centre without scrolling.
Every row, one under the other.
Small swatches in columns, for a long legend.

LayerItem.description:
An instance owned by a layer (public transport inside a sun study, a data visual on a
slide). It has no button: it comes on and goes off with its layer.

active.description: Whether it comes on when its layer opens.

stack.description:
For an item of a revealing layer (an X-ray glass, a Reveal line, #606): `1` puts it in the
surface stack, shown outside the glass or on the other side of the line; `2` (or none) in
the stack underneath, shown through it.

Steps.description: How Next moves through a layer (`docs/contracts/present.md`, Steps).

loop.description: After the last step, back to the first.

reveal.description: What Next does when a step's sub-steps (category reveals, staged builds) are done.

transition.description: How a sequence goes from one step to the next, unless a step says otherwise (#43).

sequence.description:
The steps of a sequence: other instances shown one after another. Only for layers
whose layer.json says `"sequence": true`, such as the slideshow.

oneOf.description: Next stops at the last sub-step; moving on needs Shift+Next (the Chalmers demo).
Next moves on to the next step after the last sub-step.

StepTransition.description:
How a sequence goes from one step to the next (#43). `Fade` cross-fades the two layers;
`Dip` fades the old one out to the empty map, then the new one in.

SequenceStep.description:
One step of a sequence. It shows another instance: a layer of the scene (which keeps its
own button) or one of the sequence's own items (which exist only inside it).

layer.description: The instance id this step shows.

params.description: Params the instance takes for this step only, such as another hour of the day.

duration_s.description: How long the step stays in timed mode.

next.description: Overrides the sequence's `reveal` for this step.

title.description: For the controller's info strip. The table never shows them.

notes.description:
What the guide says at this step (#98). Shown on the guide's phone and in the editor,
never on the table or the visitors' controller.

CustomLayer.description:
A custom layer: a recipe of blocks the layer editor saves (#38), run by the runtime
without code of its own. data, then look, motion and interaction, in that order.

data.description: What it shows: datasets of the site, files in the site, or map services.

look.description: How each dataset is drawn (2D only): points, lines, fills, rasters and their styles.

motion.description: What moves: reveals, pulses, particles, attractors, time.

interaction.description: What a visitor can do: tap, step, pointer.

enter.description: How the layer comes onto the table and leaves it.

controls.description: Controls, as in layer.json. A control's `bind` names the block prop it drives: `look.<block id>.<prop>`.

RecipeData.description: One source of a custom layer. Exactly one of `dataset`, `path`, `wms` and `tiles`.

dataset.description: A named dataset of the site (`data`, or the scene's buildings, trees and terrain).

path.description: A file in the site folder: GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, CSV points, an image or a video.

tiles.description: An XYZ tile URL template with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`.

Wms.description:
A WMS map. Sign-in, when the service needs it, comes from the app's Sources manager by
`source`; nothing secret is in the site.

RecipeBlock.description: One block in a custom layer's recipe. The block names are the SDK's (docs/blocks.md).

id.description: Names the block so controls and other blocks can refer to it.

data.description: The data it draws or reads, by `data[].id`.

on.description: For motion and interaction: the look block it acts on.

LegendItem.description: One row of a layer's legend on the controller (present.md, Stage).

Attract.description: The effect behind a layer on the controller's attract loop (present.md, Button).

Palette.description:
The table's palette: one of the built-in sets the SDK knows (`night` when missing) and
the slots this table overrides, by slot name, as `#rrggbb`. Layers and custom layers
refer to slots (`@accent`, `@cat3`), so changing the palette recolours them all.

Service.description: One outside service (#278). Exactly one of `run` and `url`. Contract in docs/contracts/site.md.

id.description: What layers call it by: `requires.services` and `ctx.service(id)`.

name.description: Its name for people, in the operator's view. Default: the id.

run.description: A program the host starts with the table and keeps running.

url.description: A service that runs elsewhere, such as `https://ecom.example.org`. The host forwards to it.

health.description: The path that answers 200 when the service is ready. Default `/`.

ServiceRun.description: How the host starts a service of this site.

cwd.description: Its folder, relative to the site, for example `services/ecom`.

command.description:
The program and its arguments. `{port}` is the port the host picked for it, and
`{python}` the Python of `venv` (or of this computer when there is none).

venv.description:
A virtual environment, relative to `cwd`, for example `.venv`. The host makes it on the
first start when it is missing, and installs `requirements` into it.

requirements.description: A requirements file, relative to `cwd`, installed when the venv is made or the file changed.

env.description: Extra environment variables. `{port}` is filled in here too. Keys go in Sources and keys, never here.

start_s.description: Seconds the service may take to answer its health path after it starts. Default 60.

welcome.description: The line under the title on the controller's home screen, for visitors (#73).

languages.description:
The languages visitors can switch between (#80), the first the table starts in:
`["en", "sv"]`. Empty or one language: no switch.

translations.description:
The site's own words in other languages, by language and then by the English text:
`{ "sv": { "Sample district": "Exempelstadsdelen" } }`. Titles, the welcome line, button
names, slide titles and the like. A layer's own words are in its package (`locales/`).

DataLicence.description: A `site.json` `data_licences` entry: the terms of some of the table's files.

files.description: Site-relative paths. A path ending in `/` or `*` covers everything under it.

source.description: Who it came from, such as "Lantmäteriet" or "SGU".

licence.description: The licence, such as "CC0", "ODbL-1.0", "CC BY 4.0" or "FUK".

attribution.description: The credit to show, such as "© Lantmäteriet".

share.description: Whether it may travel with the table. Worked out from the licence when left out.

Share.description: Whether a file may leave this computer with the table.

oneOf.description: Free to share, with its credit shown wherever the table is shown.
Not to be shared: it stays on this computer (an FUK agreement, a private dataset).
